newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up slightly, trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up slightly, trend unclear.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed slightly higher in moderate trade, shrugging off a move by the Central Bank to close 15 financial institutions for alleged fraudulent activities, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active stocks .BVSP ended up 0.20 percent to close at 87,195. Volume was moderate at 567.6 million reais ($541.5 million).
Although the market traded down slightly in early afternoon following the Central Bank's closing of 15 investment houses, it quickly rallied back.

"So far this investigation has only touched small banks and brokerages and no large banks or big shots in the government have been affected. If that happens then we may have a problem," one trader said.
Investors resisted temptations to take more profits following a court ruling against the government on Wednesday that prompted a moderate sell-off.

Traders noted that the market's trend was unclear due to uncertainty over the outcome of an upcoming supreme court vote on cellular privatizations and the speed with which Brasilia will be able to push its re-election bill through Congress.
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares rose 1.01 percent to close at 100.20 and common shares were unchanged at 97.50.

Traders said Petrobras shares took a hit following reports the company would have to pay a 150 million reais fine within 72 hours to alcohol fuel producers. Petrobras preferred shares fell 1.86 percent to close at 211 and common shares were down 1.08 percent at 183.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) closed virtually flat, rising just 0.02 percent to end at 2,490 points. The index includes the nine most liquid power stocks.
